summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional teachers Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, and Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyāyācārya, as well as Gopinath Bhattacharya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ishikawa Normal School, Fourth Higher School under Tokiyoshi Hōjō, the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz, and Kyoto University, later serving as professor of philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda (b. 1938) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate under Ludwig Alsdorf in 1973. He held posts as professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and director at the Shitennoji Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Otani University (1927–1931) under Enga Teramoto, later holding posts at Higashi Honganji Kobe Betsuin (1935) and Hyanghwa Girls' Vocational School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki (1897–1945) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida around 1917–1920. He later held academic posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University around 1925–1927.

Kiyoshi Okano works in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He has held posts at Kyushu University as an associate professor (attested 2002) and as professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe specializes in Buddhist studies, completing doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He held positions at Rissho University (attested 1990, and as lecturer in 2001) and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi (1906–2000) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1926–1929), he held long-term posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura (b. 1940) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo, later serving at the University of Tokyo (1983–2001) and as president of Tsurumi Women's University (~2002–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu (b. 1955) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2019), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama (b. 1928) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Takatsu, and at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn (1928–2016) was an Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf. He served as professor of Indian philology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1994.

Klaus Butzenberger (b. 1964) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He taught at Munich, Freie Universität Berlin, and Humboldt University before holding a chair at Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen (b. 1951) is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto, Asko Parpola, Henrik Zilliacus, Holger Thesleff, and Maarit Kaimio. He held appointments at the University of Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

Klaus Ludwig Janert (1922–1994) was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt under Paul Thieme, and Tübingen. He served as an assistant at the University of Göttingen (~1955–1958) and as full professor at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius (1930–2025) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Leipzig. He held teaching posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth (1990–1994), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as postdoctoral teaching staff in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn (b. 1938) is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain, later holding professorships at Giessen and Göttingen.
Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker and held a position as Dozent at the University of Münster (attested 1978).
